verdict.desc: Risk is stabilizing but not safe. Trump ruled out immediate strikes on Iran over the weekend and oil fell ~2% — WTI back near $101, Brent ~$114–115 — while S&P/Nasdaq/Dow futures edged higher after two straight weekly losses. But VIX still sits near 19.5 (top fifth of its range), Brent remains near a six-month high, and the FOMC decision lands Wednesday 10/28 inside any normal DTE, which locks out a GREEN verdict. The scanner boarded a single name — CUBI (Type A, graded B+, tagged bearish) — but the catalyst is 2 trading days old and, critically, the Oct 22 PM print was a double beat that gapped the stock UP ~6%, which conflicts with the bearish tag the scanner copied. On a Fed-week tape with an unresolved oil tail, the disciplined answer is stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past Wednesday.

focus.jnote: The environment is stabilizing but far from clear. US stock index futures ticked higher on Monday as crude oil prices retreated from last week's surge, lifting sentiment at the start of a week dominated by corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision. WTI dropped 2.16% to ~$101.04 and Brent declined 1.89% to ~$114.51 as reports of Qatari diplomatic efforts to ease US–Iran tensions pressured prices, although continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply risks elevated. Over the weekend US gold prices rose as oil prices fell and President Trump stated, “There will be no strikes today” on Sunday. Volatility stays bid: the market regime is neutral and choppy, with the VIX at 19.45, the cash curve in contango and SKEW elevated at 151.80. This is a Fed-week tape with an unresolved oil tail — not a clean premium-selling backdrop.
focus.notdown: CUBI is the only boarded name — and it's a messy one. Customers Bancorp reported Q3 earnings of $2.25 per share, or $2.27 adjusted for non-recurring costs. The results exceeded Wall Street expectations — the average estimate of eight analysts was $2.15 per share. A double beat that drove the stock up 5.92% (to ~$83.39) on Oct 23 is a bullish gap-up setup — yet the scanner copied it as bearish. We keep the row per the hard rules but flag the direction conflict and the near-zero relative volume. Watch-only on a RED day.
focus.notup: No clean bear-call candidate boarded today. The scanner's lone name (CUBI) is tagged bearish but the earnings reaction was a gap UP, so there is no coherent bear-call thesis to sell into. Selling bear calls into a VIX-near-19.5, FOMC-week tape invites a squeeze on any dovish-Fed or de-escalation headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~62 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at ~42% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. On top of that, the Fed, ECB and Bank of Japan announce rate decisions Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, with fed funds futures showing a ~90% chance of a hold though Bank of America expects a quarter-point hike. A live FOMC inside any normal DTE is an automatic stand-down trigger, and the lone boarded setup is stale (2 sessions) and direction-conflicted. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past Wednesday and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Boarded Type A, graded B+, tagged bearish — but the print and the tape both argue the other way. Customers Bancorp reported Q3 EPS of $2.25 ($2.27 adjusted), beating the ~$2.15 consensus of eight analysts. Record total deposits of $22.6 billion (up 11% YoY) and total loans of $18.5 billion (up 14% YoY) accompanied the beat. The stock then rose 5.92% to ~$83.39 on Oct 23 — a gap UP, which contradicts the scanner's bearish tag. The scanner's own notes flag the weak spots: relative volume 0.01× (far below the 1.3× bar), an implied move of 7.8% vs a realized gap it logged at −5.6%, no open-interest data returned, and the catalyst is now 2 trading days old (reported 10/22 PM). On a RED, FOMC-week day this is watch-only at most — and the direction conflict alone is a reason to pass.
setups.check_note: Do not open new premium on a RED day, and resolve the direction conflict first: the scanner says bearish, but CUBI gapped UP ~6% on a double beat, so a bear call is fighting the tape. Relative volume (0.01×) is the weak spot and the gap is 2 sessions old, so any fresh move may already be stale/filled. If you somehow build a bull-put instead, confirm at 9:35 that price > prior close AND > today's open AND in the upper third of range — and verify open interest and ATM spread manually (none returned). FOMC Wed 10/28 is inside a normal DTE; next earnings ~Jan 28, 2027.

risks: FOMC · Wed 10/28 — fed funds futures show a 90% chance of a hold, but Bank of America expects a quarter-point hike. A hawkish surprise inside any normal DTE is the week's number-one scheduled gap risk — keep every spread clear of Wednesday.
ECB (Thu) & BoJ (Fri) — the Fed, ECB and Bank of Japan announce rate decisions Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. A back-to-back central-bank gauntlet can whipsaw rates, the dollar and risk all week.

Oil & Strait of Hormuz — continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep supply risks elevated even as Brent eases from a six-month high. Any shipping incident sends crude vertical again — the biggest open-ended tail.

AI / mega-cap earnings — AI stocks struggled after last week's sell-off, with Alphabet and Microsoft reporting earnings on Wednesday as investors weigh growing AI spending and backlogs. A disappointing hyperscaler print could re-crack the whole index.

Thin, stale, direction-conflicted lone setup — CUBI printed on near-zero relative volume (0.01×), the catalyst is 2 sessions old, and the scanner's bearish tag contradicts the stock's ~6% gap UP on a double beat. Treat it as a watch-only item, not a tradeable spread, on a RED day.
